title: Evicting children from a parent's own property - an underused remedy
p1:
Can a parent legally ask their own child to leave the house?

Many people assume the answer is always no. But the law may provide a remedy when a parent's own property becomes a place of neglect, abuse, or constant harassment.
p2: A common misconception is that children automatically get a permanent right to stay in their parents' self-acquired property. In reality, a parent who owns the property may have the right to seek eviction, especially when the child's presence affects the parent's safety, dignity, or peace of mind.
p3:
The process depends on the facts and the applicable law, but the key point is often overlooked: ownership rights do not disappear simply because the person occupying the property is a family member. Many parents tolerate difficult situations because they are unaware that legal remedies exist.

Knowing your rights can help families address conflicts before they become more serious.
conclusion: Did you know that a parent may have legal options to remove a child from their own property? Should more people be aware of this remedy?
